currentContext.strengths: Multisensor mobile mapping capabilities, an expanding digital twin portfolio, and growing engagement with urban local bodies and state governments across India, positioning the Company within the industry's shift from map production to intelligence products.|A rich repository of high-definition and 3D spatial data built through years of pioneering work in India, described as a differentiated asset positioning the Company within the emerging Physical AI landscape.|Genesys Map Stack as a proprietary integrated data foundation combining imagery, LiDAR, navigable road networks, street-level imagery, terrain models and 3D city data.|First-mover technical credentials: India's first large-scale HD ADAS maps covering more than 1 lakh kilometres of highways at centimetre-level accuracy using the Survey of India CORS network, and India's first comprehensive 3D subsurface mapping programme across six airports.|Hybrid computing architecture combining scalable cloud processing with secure on-premises infrastructure, addressing data sovereignty and security requirements of government clients.|Long-duration contracted revenue: a six-year Tata Motors contract compensated as a licence fee per vehicle sold.|Standards influence through participation in the BIS LITD 22 technical committee shaping OGC compliance for government-funded platforms.|Scale, technical depth and track record cited by management as competitive differentiation against price-based competition in government tenders.|Structured learning and development programmes cited as a sustained competitive advantage in talent retention and delivery quality in a sector facing a skilled-professional shortage.
currentContext.strategies: Build a balanced portfolio of data, products, platforms and solutions, with continued focus on Government, utilities and infrastructure, automotive and mobility, and location intelligence for commercial and enterprise customers.|Keep the Genesys Map Stack central as the foundation for Digital Twin, GeoAI and location intelligence applications.|Convert geospatial assets and domain expertise into products and platforms, progressively embedding GeoAI, machine learning, analytics and location intelligence to enable automated insights, monitoring, prediction and decision support.|Modernise survey and data acquisition with advanced sensing, notably high-resolution Ground Penetrating Radar for subsurface utility detection, and extend it from airport environments to city-scale underground utility mapping so that Digital Twins span underground, surface and above-ground infrastructure.|Increase automation across processing and production workflows on a hybrid computing architecture combining scalable cloud processing with secure on-premises infrastructure, to improve efficiency, scalability and turnaround time while meeting data security and sovereignty requirements.|Strengthen the international business by leveraging capabilities in advanced surveying, mapping, Digital Twins, automotive mapping and AI-led spatial intelligence.|Expand into in-vehicle navigation and ADAS for software-defined vehicles, building out the automotive mapping stack.|Exploit the Physical AI opportunity created by the Company's repository of high-definition and 3D spatial data, including Generative AI and Agentic AI applications across industries.|Participate in standards-setting through the BIS LITD 22 technical committee shaping OGC compliance for government-funded geospatial platforms.
currentContext.expansion: Genesys is an asset-light geospatial services company and discloses no manufacturing plants; BRSR Section A records 'Not Applicable' for plants and lists 5 national and 2 international offices, with development centres and offices in Mumbai (SEEPZ and Kanjurmarg), New Delhi, Jaipur and Kolkata. Expansion in FY 2025-26 was capability- and footprint-led rather than plant-led. The Company modernised its survey and data acquisition capabilities by adopting advanced sensing technologies, including high-resolution Ground Penetrating Radar for subsurface utility detection and mapping, launching India's first advanced GPR solution from IDS GeoRadar with patented Equalised Scrambling Technology and Wide/Multi Array Antenna Technology; the Chairman states that, beginning with airport environments, the Company plans to progressively extend this capability to city-scale underground utility mapping. Mapping operations were scaled through greater automation across processing and production workflows on a hybrid computing architecture combining scalable cloud processing with secure on-premises infrastructure, addressing data sovereignty and security requirements. Map-asset build-out included India's first large-scale HD ADAS maps launched in December 2025 covering more than 1 lakh kilometres of national highways, expressways and strategic road corridors, built as part of the New India Map Stack and leveraging the Survey of India CORS network for centimetre-level accuracy. Geographic expansion included the first project in North-East India (a Rs 13 crore Urban Digital Twin Map Platform for Guwahati), a Rs 9.13 crore Digital Twin for the Kochi Municipal Corporation, and a Rs 17.38 crore Bureau Veritas-awarded 3D subsurface mapping programme across six Adani Group airports (Mumbai, Trivandrum, Lucknow, Jaipur, Guwahati, Ahmedabad). The Directors' Report records QIP proceeds from the 17-05-2025 issue earmarked against stated objects including setting up of a data centre, development of a tech platform, creation/updation of map content, building sensor capacity and strengthening information technology infrastructure, with no deviation or variation in utilisation from the stated objects; as at the reporting date the data centre, map content and sensor capacity objects were still substantially undrawn while the tech platform object had begun drawing down. Capacity growth is also human: the Company hired 133 professionals during the year and reports a headcount of 947 professionals as at 31 March 2026 (BRSR separately reports 802 permanent and 1,201 total employees). BRSR reports environmental/social-purpose capex of Nil in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
